title: Annotatio V §.IV: reply to first — double elenchus + double petitio; Oral nowhere clear in Scripture
pass_a_gloss: To which Reply to the first: It labors both with a double Elenchus and with a double Petition of the principle. With a double Elenchus indeed: For it is not disputed either about this — Whether it is a matter of great moment or not to call into doubt a Doctrine clearly and perspicuously set forth in Scripture and likewise to detract faith from Christ’s words, which is to make Christ a liar and so to involve oneself in a sin of greatest moment; Nor: Whether Oral Eating is of great moment or not? which if true, by Divine truth — i.e. Truth manifested by GOD, declared by Christ Himself — cannot but by that very fact be of great moment; but only this is now being examined: Whether, given the Truth of Oral Eating, even Divine, and so of great moment, it is of so great moment that, denied, the foundation of the Christian Religion is shaken: or, to speak more clearly, whether a dogma is denied which by GOD’s and Christ’s own judgment is absolutely necessary to obtaining salvation? And likewise, whether such a Dogma is denied which as it separates the denier from GOD and Christ, so excludes him from the Saints’ ecclesiastical communion? No less does the First labor with a double petition of the principle: For it is most of all in question: (1) That the Oral Eating of Christ’s Body is a Doctrine clearly and perspicuously set forth in Scripture — seeing it is nowhere read set forth. Certainly in these Institution words of the Sacred Supper: Eat, this is my Body, it is not more clearly set forth than in Christ’s words John 6. Unless one eats the Flesh of the Son of man, he has no life in himself — in which yet the Lutherans themselves deny that it is set forth. (2) That Christ pronounced of the whole complex, or Complex of bread and Body: Eat, this is my Body — when such a Complex never existed nor will ever exist; But Christ pronounced of the bread taken in hand, blessed, broken, handed to the Disciples’ hands: This is my Body, in altogether the same mode of pronouncing in which a little later He pronounced: This cup is the New Testament in my blood — i.e. in a tropical or figurative mode of pronouncing, which yet does not take away the most true presence of Christ’s Body in the Supper, while it admits only the Spiritual, seeing it was enjoined to be eaten only in a spiritual mode, not another, John 6 — as is uncontested.
pass_b_english: Reply to (1): double elenchus + double petitio. The live question is not whether doubting clear Scripture or a truly divine Oral would be grave, but whether Oral — even if true — is so necessary that denying it shakes the Christian foundation / excludes from the saints’ communion.

Petitio: Oral is nowhere clearly set in Scripture — ‘Eat, this is my Body’ is no clearer for Oral than John 6, which Lutherans themselves deny teaches Oral. Nor did Christ pronounce of a bread+body complex that never exists; He spoke of the bread tropically, as of the cup as New Testament — without canceling most-true spiritual presence (Jn 6).
source_text: Cui Resp. ad primum: Tùm Elenchô duplici, tùm duplici principii Petitione laborare. Elenchô quidem duplici: Neque enim disceptatur, vel de eo; Utrum res magni momenti sit, nec ne, Doctrinam in Scriptura clarè & perspicuè propositam, vocare in dubium itemque, verbis Christi fidem detrahere, quod est Christum facere mendacem, eóque se maximi momenti peccato implicare; Nec: Utrum Oralis Manducatio magni momenti sit, nec ne? quæ si vera, veritate Divinâ, i. e. Veritate à DEO manifestatâ, à Christo ipso indicta, non potest non eô ipsô magni momenti esse; sed de eo solummodò nunc dispicitur: Utrum, datâ Oralis Manducationis Veritate, etiam Divinâ, eóque magni momenti, tanti ista momenti sit, ut negata, fundamentum Christianæ Religionis concutiatur: vel, ut clarius loquar, dogma negetur, ipsius DEI Christique judicio, ad salutem consequendam absolutè necessarium? Itemque, negetur tale Dogma, quod uti sejungit negantem à DEO Christóque, ita communione Sanctorum ecclesiasticâ excludit? Non minùs verò duplici petitione principii Primum laborat: In quæstione enim est quam maximè: (1) Oralem Corporis Christi Manducationem esse Doctrinam clarè & perspicuè in Scriptura propositam; quandoquidem nullibi proposita legitur. Certe in Institutionis S. Cœnæ verbis hisce: Edite, hoc est Corpus meum, non clariùs proposita est, quàm in Verbis Christi Joh. 6. Nisi quis comederit Carnem Filii hominis, non habet vitam in se, in quibus tamen eam proponi, ipsimet Lutherani inficiantur. (2) Christum de toto sympeplegmenô, seu Complexo ex pane & Corpore, pronunciasse: Edite hoc est Corpus meum; cùm tale Complexum nunquam exstiterit, nec exstiturum unquam sit; Pronunciaverit verò Christus de pane, in manus accepto, benedicto, fracto, Discipulorum manibus tradito: Hoc est Corpus meum, eodem prorsus pronunciandi modo, quo paulò post pronunciabat: Hoc poculum est Novum Testamentum in sanguine meo, i. e. pronunciandi modo tropicô seu figuratô, qui tamen non tollat præsentiam Corporis Christi in Cœna verissimam, Spiritualem interim admittat tantùm, utpote spirituali duntaxat, non aliô, modô manducari injuncti Joh. 6. uti inconfesso est.
notes: Reply to first: elenchus + petitio; not clear in Scripture.
